To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a highly efficient and linear fully-integrated Ga-N power amplifier (PA), with an output 1dB compression point of POUT, 3dB = 32 dBm at 15 GHz, is proposed for 5G mobile communications.

we have developed a 15 GHz fully integrated GaN power amplifier that achieves 32.2dBm of output 1dB compression power with 30.0 percent of power-added-efficiency (PAE) and 28.2dB of gain, and that this power amplifier is highly linear and can pass the LTE spectrum emission masks for 5 MHz to20 MHz LTE signals without any predistorters.
we have designed and simulated a highly efficient and linear two-stage 15GHz GaN power amplifier for 5G applications.

The main takeaway from our work is that
GaN PAs can be very efficient at 15 GHz and that the efficiency is not necessarily sacrificed to achieve linearity.
a two-stage PA design with a low-gain first stage and a high-gain second stage can achieve a high PAE at high output power, and this design is also linear enough for 5G LTE signals.
a two-stage GaN PA design is quite suitable for 5G wireless communications at 15 GHz, and it may also be suitable for other high frequency wireless communications.
